committees.name: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal financial regulatory agencies, new depository institution applicants, credit unions, and state regulators.
dimensions.evidence: Each of the Federal financial institutions regulatory agencies shall... review and streamline the application process for the formation of de novo, or new, depository institutions or credit unions.

dimensions.assessment: Streamlines administrative procedures, creates assistance programs, and reviews capital-raising rules without altering primary banking laws fundamentally.
dimensions.evidence: conduct a review of any application forms related to such process

dimensions.assessment: Includes a $24,000,000 reduction in the Federal Reserve discretionary surplus fund effective in 2036.
dimensions.evidence: The dollar amount specified under section 7(a)(3)(A) of the Federal Reserve Act is reduced by $24,000,000.

dimensions.assessment: Requires multiple federal regulatory agencies to create caseworkers, mentorship programs, state engagement plans, and periodic reports.
dimensions.evidence: Each of the Federal financial institutions regulatory agencies shall, at the request of an applicant... designate an employee... as a caseworker

dimensions.assessment: Requires ongoing reports, recurring state engagement plans, and a long-term adjustment to the Federal Reserve surplus fund taking effect in 2036.

missing_information: Administrative costs incurred by individual agencies in setting up the required mentorship directories and engagement plans.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs federal financial regulators to streamline de novo banking and credit union application processes, review capital raising rules, establish caseworkers and mentor programs, and develop stakeholder engagement plans, supported by a minor reduction in the Federal Reserve discretionary surplus fund.

card.label: H.R. 6644
card.summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies federal housing programs and banking regulations to address housing supply, affordability, and regulatory hurdles. It creates pilot programs and grant initiatives for housing repairs, conversions of empty buildings, small-dollar mortgages, and manufactured housing without permanent chassis. It also adjusts environmental review rules under NEPA, alters bank investment limits, modifies the HOME Investment Partnerships program, and restricts the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency.
